cross_engine_notes: Ghidra and IDA static analysis failed entirely due to tooling errors (Ghidra project ownership conflict, missing IDA SQL utility), so no function, import, or decompilation data is available from those engines. All successfully executed tools (capa, pe_imports, YARA, FLOSS) provide consistent evidence of malicious characteristics: UPX packing, anti-VM functionality, and imports of high-risk APIs associated with process injection and memory manipulation, enabling high-confidence malicious classification despite the lack of unpacked payload analysis.

key_evidence.row_or_rule: packed with UPX (ATT&CK T1027.002, MBC F0001.008)
key_evidence.why: Confirms the sample is packed with UPX, a common packer used to obfuscate malware and evade static analysis, mapped to the Defense Evasion tactic (Software Packing subtechnique).

These high-signal Windows APIs are commonly used by malware for dynamic API resolution, memory allocation, and modification of memory protection to enable process injection and execution of malicious code, mapped to ATT&CK T1055 (Process Injection) and T1129 (Execution through API).
Indicates the sample contains logic to detect virtualized/sandbox environments, a common anti-analysis technique used by malware to avoid detection in security research environments.

key_evidence.row_or_rule: Multiple UPX-related YARA rule matches (UPX, UPXv20MarkusLaszloReiser, UPX_290_LZMA, etc.)
key_evidence.why: Independently confirms the sample is packed with UPX, consistent with capa's packing detection finding.
No decoded or stack strings were extracted, which is consistent with packed/obfuscated malware that hides its true functionality and strings until unpacked in memory.

summary: This is a UPX-packed Windows PE file with multiple confirmed malicious indicators: packing for obfuscation (Defense Evasion T1027.002), anti-VM detection, and imports of APIs used for process injection and memory manipulation. Static analysis via Ghidra and IDA failed due to tooling issues, but cross-engine evidence from capa, pe_imports, YARA, and FLOSS provides high confidence the sample is malicious. The underlying payload is hidden by UPX packing and requires unpacking for further analysis and family attribution.
